{"id": "3:37/q11", "question": "Who is grammatically the agent of Mary's guardianship?", "turns_on": "The light verb makes Zakariya subject; the doubled or hamza causative makes God subject and Zakariya object.", "positions": [{"id": "3:37/q11/p1", "position": "God assigned Mary to Zakariya: doubled kaffalahā makes Zakariya accusative.", "reasons": "Kufan readers use the causative; Ṭabarī prefers it because the lot in 3:44 displays God’s judgment. The verb takes Mary and Zakariya as two objects; Ubayy's akfalahā has the same force."}, {"id": "3:37/q11/p2", "position": "Zakariya himself undertook her care: light kafalahā makes him nominative subject.", "reasons": "Hijazi, Medinan and Basran readers use it, supported by 3:44; Jishumī and Rāzī prefer it as the majority reading. Ṭabarī counters that 3:44 does not force it."}, {"id": "3:37/q11/p3", "position": "A light form with kasra on fāʾ likewise makes Zakariya the agent.", "reasons": "Akhfash and later readers report the dialect kafila; Samīn says its syntax follows the other light reading."}, {"id": "3:37/q11/p4", "position": "Ubayy reads a hamza causative, wa-akfalahā, with God as agent.", "reasons": "Zamakhsharī, Qurtubī, Samīn and others treat it like the doubled two-object construction."}]}
{"id": "3:37/q12", "question": "How is Zakariya's name read and inflected?", "turns_on": "Long hamzated and short forms are established readings; a third declinable form is Arabic usage but outside the codex.", "positions": [{"id": "3:37/q12/p1", "position": "The name is long and hamzated; in light-verb readings it is nominative, and in Abū Bakr’s doubled reading accusative.", "reasons": "Ṭabarī calls long and short equally valid; Abū Bakr from ʿĀṣim combines the long name with the causative and accusative."}, {"id": "3:37/q12/p2", "position": "A third, declinable Zakari or Zakariyy form occurs in Arabic dialects, but is not recited here.", "reasons": "Farrāʾ calls it Najdi; Fārisī explains substituted nisba yāʾs. Ṭabarī and Zajjāj exclude it from recitation because of rasm. Akhfash also records Zakar."}, {"id": "3:37/q12/p3", "position": "The name is shortened without the final hamza, especially with the doubled verb.", "reasons": "Ḥafṣ, Ḥamza, Kisāʾī and Khalaf commonly shorten throughout the Qurʾān; Ṭabarī accepts both dialects without change in meaning."}]}
{"id": "3:37/q13", "question": "Why is the name Zakariya indeclinable in its long and short forms?", "turns_on": "Whether the operative cause is the fused feminine alif or foreign proper-name status.", "positions": [{"id": "3:37/q13/p1", "position": "Its fused final feminine alif prevents declension even when indefinite.", "reasons": "Zajjāj, Naḥḥās and Fārisī distinguish alif from removable feminine tāʾ; indefinite indeclinability is their evidence against Abū Ḥātim."}, {"id": "3:37/q13/p2", "position": "It is indeclinable because it is a foreign proper name.", "reasons": "Ibn Khalawayh gives this rule; Zajjāj and Naḥḥās report and dispute the explanation, especially for the indefinite form."}]}
{"id": "3:37/q14", "question": "When and why did Zakariya become Mary's guardian?", "turns_on": "Whether the first lot chose custody in infancy, a later famine lot assigned maintenance, or custody began after weaning.", "positions": [{"id": "3:37/q14/p1", "position": "The priests competed for infant Mary; a lot selected Zakariya as guardian.", "reasons": "She was their leader’s daughter and vowed to temple service; Zakariya claimed kinship through her aunt. Ṭabarī, Ibn ʿAṭiyya, Ibn al-Jawzī and others prefer the common early-lot account."}, {"id": "3:37/q14/p2", "position": "Zakariya first cared for her as an orphan without a lot; famine later brought a lottery for her maintenance, won by carpenter Jurayj.", "reasons": "Ibn Isḥāq says this contest relieved Zakariya’s inability to support her; Ibn ʿAṭiyya distinguishes a custody lottery from an expense lottery; Ibn Kathīr sees compatible circumstances."}, {"id": "3:37/q14/p3", "position": "Zakariya took custody only after Mary was weaned.", "reasons": "Rāzī reports an argument from the apparent sequence of growth before care; the majority answer that waw need not mark temporal order."}]}
{"id": "3:37/q15", "question": "What happened to Zakariya's pen in the lot?", "turns_on": "Reports differ on whether it moved upstream, remained upright, or floated while the others sank.", "positions": [{"id": "3:37/q15/p1", "position": "His pen floated or rose above water while the others sank.", "reasons": "Ibn Isḥāq and later reports use this sign, with some accounts repeating the trial three times."}, {"id": "3:37/q15/p2", "position": "It stood still or upright as if fixed in clay while other pens drifted.", "reasons": "Al-Suddī places the contest in the Jordan; another report says the pen stayed upright on its points."}, {"id": "3:37/q15/p3", "position": "It moved upstream while the others followed the current.", "reasons": "Reports from ʿIkrima and others say this sign gave him the strongest claim."}]}
{"id": "3:37/q16", "question": "How many priests drew lots for Mary?", "turns_on": "The reported number is twenty-seven or twenty-nine.", "positions": [{"id": "3:37/q16/p1", "position": "Twenty-seven men cast pens.", "reasons": "Zamakhsharī and several successors give this number."}, {"id": "3:37/q16/p2", "position": "Twenty-nine men cast lots.", "reasons": "Thaʿlabī, Baghawī and Ṭabrisī give this number."}]}
{"id": "3:37/q17", "question": "Where and with what did the priests draw lots?", "turns_on": "Jordan versus a spring; Torah pens versus wooden staffs or named lots.", "positions": [{"id": "3:37/q17/p1", "position": "They cast Torah-writing pens into the Jordan.", "reasons": "Al-Suddī names the river; some reports say pens carried priests’ names, others stress that they wrote the Torah."}, {"id": "3:37/q17/p2", "position": "The lots were wooden staffs or pens cast in a spring or other flowing water.", "reasons": "Ibn ʿAṭiyya records variation in material and location; Abū Ḥayyān records a nearby spring."}]}
{"id": "3:37/q18", "question": "What was Zakariya's family relationship to Mary?", "turns_on": "Whether his wife was Mary's aunt, Mary's sister, or another maternal relative.", "positions": [{"id": "3:37/q18/p1", "position": "His wife was Mary's maternal aunt, mother of Yahya.", "reasons": "Ibn Isḥāq and many sources say this gave him a claim to custody; Shuʿayb names the aunt Ashiʿ; Ibn Kathīr invokes the legal analogy that an aunt is like a mother."}, {"id": "3:37/q18/p2", "position": "His wife was Mary's sister, another daughter of Imran.", "reasons": "Al-Suddī and others cite the Prophet’s designation of John and Jesus as sons of maternal aunts; Ibn ʿĀshūr disputes that she was a sister."}, {"id": "3:37/q18/p3", "position": "She was a maternal relative, likely an aunt, without a definite sister relationship.", "reasons": "Luke calls Elisabeth Mary's relative; Ibn ʿĀshūr prefers an aunt or maternal relative; Study Quran leaves the exact relation open."}]}
{"id": "3:37/q19", "question": "What lineage and identity is given for Zakariya?", "turns_on": "Solomon and David’s line versus Aaron’s line.", "positions": [{"id": "3:37/q19/p1", "position": "Zakariya was son of Ādhan son of Muslim, descending from Solomon and David.", "reasons": "Baghawī and later sources give this chain, with minor variation in the next ancestor's name."}, {"id": "3:37/q19/p2", "position": "He belonged to Aaron’s priestly descent, not Solomon’s line.", "reasons": "Abū al-Barakāt al-Juwānī distinguishes the lines of Levi and Judah; Ibn ʿĀshūr follows Luke's priestly house of Abijah."}]}
{"id": "3:37/q20", "question": "How was Mary housed and cared for?", "turns_on": "Reports vary on the chamber, wet nurse, locked doors, visits, and whether she left during menstruation.", "positions": [{"id": "3:37/q20/p1", "position": "Zakariya built an elevated sanctuary chamber reached by ladder, arranged her nourishment, and limited entry.", "reasons": "Ibn Isḥāq says she first stayed with her aunt; Muqātil and other reports mention a wet nurse and a raised doorway."}, {"id": "3:37/q20/p2", "position": "She was secluded behind locked doors; Zakariya alone entered.", "reasons": "Al-Rabīʿ and others count seven doors; Muqātil says he kept the key and brought supplies."}, {"id": "3:37/q20/p3", "position": "During menstruation Zakariya sent her to a female relative and returned her after purification.", "reasons": "Muqātil says this relative was his sister or Mary’s aunt, mother of Yahya."}, {"id": "3:37/q20/p4", "position": "Mary did not menstruate.", "reasons": "Qurtubī and Abū Ḥayyān report this alternative."}]}
{"id": "3:37/q21", "question": "What does miḥrāb denote here?", "turns_on": "A private elevated chamber, a mosque or its honored front, or a palace-like honored space.", "positions": [{"id": "3:37/q21/p1", "position": "Mary’s elevated private chamber or worship room in the sanctuary.", "reasons": "Al-Aṣmaʿī cites 38:21 and poetry about ladder access; Wāḥidī, Elmalılı and Kuran Yolu identify a raised temple room; Ibn ʿĀshūr distinguishes it from a mosque."}, {"id": "3:37/q21/p2", "position": "The mosque, its prayer niche, or its foremost honored section.", "reasons": "Abū ʿUbayda defines the leading seat in an assembly; Ṭabarī lists mosque and honored prayer place; Samīn prefers the familiar mosque sanctuary here."}, {"id": "3:37/q21/p3", "position": "A palace or lofty distinguished building.", "reasons": "Abū ʿAmr defines it by height and nobility; Imruʾ al-Qays and others use its plural for palaces."}]}

:37/q22/p2", "position": "It is named for rivalry over the honored place.", "reasons": "Abū Ḥayyān, Samīn and al-Ālūsī mention competition for the prayer leader’s place."}, {"id": "3:37/q22/p3", "position": "It names the front and foremost part of an honored room or assembly.", "reasons": "Rāghib favors a room’s front modeled on a mosque’s; al-Ḥarallī pictures the front of a difficult-to-reach house."}]}
{"id": "3:37/q23", "question": "How is 'entered the miḥrāb' parsed?", "turns_on": "Whether miḥrāb is a place adverb or a direct object by broadened transitivity.", "positions": [{"id": "3:37/q23/p1", "position": "Miḥrāb is an accusative place adverb despite being a specified place.", "reasons": "Sībawayh treats this as exceptional, since specified locations normally require fī; al-Ālūsī calls it expansion of dakhala."}, {"id": "3:37/q23/p2", "position": "Miḥrāb is a direct object of dakhala.", "reasons": "Akhfash offers this; Samīn rejects it because non-place senses take fī."}]}
{"id": "3:37/q24", "question": "What is the force and syntax of kullamā?", "turns_on": "Whether wajada or qāla supplies the response and governs the time expression.", "positions": [{"id": "3:37/q24/p1", "position": "Wajada is the response governing kullamā: he found provision every time he entered.", "reasons": "Zajjāj, Naḥḥās, Ibn ʿAṭiyya, Wāḥidī and Qurtubī parse mā with dakhala as a verbal noun; al-Ālūsī allows a relative analysis."}, {"id": "3:37/q24/p2", "position": "Qāla is the response; wajada is a circumstantial clause: whenever he entered having found food, he spoke.", "reasons": "Samīn prefers this analysis and rejects omitted-faʾ arguments from a poem and 6:121."}]}
{"id": "3:37/q25", "question": "What does repeated entry show?", "turns_on": "", "positions": [{"id": "3:37/q25/p1", "position": "Zakariya repeatedly checked Mary’s needs and repeatedly found God’s provision.", "reasons": "Qushayrī stresses daily visits and that saintly wonders need not be constant; Abū Ḥayyān and Biqāʿī likewise infer habitual care."}]}
{"id": "3:37/q26", "question": "Why is 'upon her' advanced before Zakariya and the miḥrāb?", "turns_on": "", "positions": [{"id": "3:37/q26/p1", "position": "The order foregrounds Mary because she is the passage’s focus.", "reasons": "Sāmarrāʾī applies Sībawayh’s rule that speakers advance what matters most; al-Ālūsī says the placement marks special concern for her."}]}
{"id": "3:37/q27", "question": "What was the provision Zakariya found?", "turns_on": "Fruit out of season, grapes or other fruit, multiplied ordinary food, knowledge, or Mary herself.", "positions": [{"id": "3:37/q27/p1", "position": "Fruit appearing out of season, often summer fruit in winter and winter fruit in summer.", "reasons": "Early reports name grapes, sometimes in a basket, and pomegranates; Ibn ʿAbbās also calls it Paradise fruit. Rāzī claims the seasonal account is widely transmitted."}, {"id": "3:37/q27/p2", "position": "Knowledge, a written page, wisdom, or spiritual realities.", "reasons": "Mujāhid and Rāghib offer knowledge or scrolls; Ibn Kathīr prefers fruit and Abū Ḥayyān calls knowledge remote; Qāshānī and al-Ālūsī give inward readings."}, {"id": "3:37/q27/p3", "position": "Ordinary food brought by a supporter was multiplied or augmented by God.", "reasons": "Ibn Isḥāq says Jurayj earned a little food and it increased inside the sanctuary; other reports mention excess beyond what a caretaker brought."}, {"id": "3:37/q27/p4", "position": "Mary herself is called the provision in one gloss.", "reasons": "Ibrāhīm b. al-Muhājir gives this reading as excerpted by Ibn Abī Ḥātim."}, {"id": "3:37/q27/p5", "position": "It was food from outside the region, including grapes not grown there.", "reasons": "Abū Ḥayyān reports a geographical explanation distinct from seasonal reversal."}]}
{"id": "3:37/q28", "question": "By what means did Mary's food arrive?", "turns_on": "Direct divine or heavenly provision versus delivery by an angel or human helper.", "positions": [{"id": "3:37/q28/p1", "position": "God supplied it directly from heaven or Paradise without human mediation.", "reasons": "Al-Ḥasan argues Zakariya would not have asked if he already knew a human source; Māwardī prefers direct provision; locked doors strengthen the inference for several authors."}, {"id": "3:37/q28/p2", "position": "A righteous person or appointed caretaker brought it.", "reasons": "Māwardī proposes a righteous servant; Ibn Isḥāq identifies carpenter Jurayj and says God increased what he delivered; al-Jubbāʾī and Rashīd Riḍā allow ordinary believers and famine."}, {"id": "3:37/q28/p3", "position": "An angel brought it from Paradise; Muqātil names Gabriel.", "reasons": "Wāḥidī and others specify angels carrying the seasonal fruit; Muqātil identifies Gabriel."}]}
{"id": "3:37/q29", "question": "When did Zakariya find the provision and when did Mary speak?", "turns_on": "Infancy before nursing versus after weaning or adult sanctuary life.", "positions": [{"id": "3:37/q29/p1", "position": "In infancy: Mary never suckled and spoke as a small child.", "reasons": "Al-Ḥasan and others compare Jesus’ cradle speech; Abū Ḥayyān notes sound reports list other infant speakers but omit Mary."}, {"id": "3:37/q29/p2", "position": "After weaning or adulthood, when Mary lived in the sanctuary.", "reasons": "Ibn Isḥāq dates the provision after maturity; Abū Ḥayyān prefers the later chronology; a report places it after she was weaned at two."}]}
{"id": "3:37/q30", "question": "What does the indefinite rizqan suggest?", "turns_on": "A strange magnificent provision or abundant variety.", "positions": [{"id": "3:37/q30/p1", "position": "It magnifies a strange, extraordinary provision.", "reasons": "Rāzī and al-Ālūsī say the indefiniteness supports the marvel; Ṭabāṭabāʾī argues ordinary temple donations would not explain the wording."}, {"id": "3:37/q30/p2", "position": "It suggests varied and abundant kinds of provision.", "reasons": "Abū Ḥayyān and Biqāʿī read the unqualified indefinite this way."}]}
{"id": "3:37/q31", "question": "What does annā ask?", "turns_on": "Whether 'from where' includes route and source, or whether the force is 'how'.", "positions": [{"id": "3:37/q31/p1", "position": "From where, that is, the source or direction of this provision.", "reasons": "Abū ʿUbayda glosses min ayna; al-Kumayt’s verse is cited; Naḥḥās distinguishes annā's route or source from ayna's location; Ibn al-Dahhān cites Mary's answer as evidence."}, {"id": "3:37/q31/p2", "position": "How did this provision come about?", "reasons": "Ibn Fāris prefers how; Ibn Qutayba says how and from where are close; Abū Ḥayyān allows it while preferring source or direction."}]}
{"id": "3:37/q32", "question": "Why did Zakariya question Mary?", "turns_on": "Surprise at inaccessible food versus concern that another person supplied it.", "positions": [{"id": "3:37/q32/p1", "position": "He was amazed by food outside its season, behind locked doors, or unlike worldly food.", "reasons": "Ṭabarī, Zajjāj, Zamakhsharī and others describe a question that reveals the marvel; several say fresh fruit was unavailable to anyone else."}, {"id": "3:37/q32/p2", "position": "He checked whether another person had provided it, perhaps improperly or before him.", "reasons": "Qushayrī says he feared being surpassed in service; Wāḥidī and Abū Ḥayyān say Mary's answer reassured him. Al-Jubbāʾī imagines concern over an illicit source; Rāzī objects that her assertion alone would not dispel suspicion."}]}
{"id": "3:37/q33", "question": "What does Mary's answer 'from God' assert?", "turns_on": "Immediate divine origin versus ultimate providence through ordinary means.", "positions": [{"id": "3:37/q33/p1", "position": "No human brought it: God sent this particular provision.", "reasons": "Ṭabarī says God sent and gave it; Ibn ʿAṭiyya argues Zakariya would not have accepted the reply otherwise; al-Ālūsī allows Paradise as its source."}, {"id": "3:37/q33/p2", "position": "It expresses Mary’s awareness that all provision ultimately comes from God.", "reasons": "Asad reads it without requiring miraculous food; Rashīd Riḍā and Kuran Yolu likewise allow ordinary human delivery."}]}
{"id": "3:37/q34", "question": "Whose extraordinary sign, if any, was Mary's provision?", "turns_on": "Whether saintly wonders occur, and if so whether this event belongs to Mary, Zakariya, or Jesus.", "positions": [{"id": "3:37/q34/p1", "position": "It was Mary's karāma, showing that extraordinary favors may occur for non-prophets.", "reasons": "Ṭabrisī, Rāzī, Abū Ḥayyān, Ibn Kathīr and al-Ālūsī argue that Zakariya’s question excludes his arranged miracle and Jesus was not yet born; Rāzī distinguishes saints’ wonders from prophets’ challenging signs."}, {"id": "3:37/q34/p2", "position": "It was a miracle for Zakariya, linked to his prayer for Mary.", "reasons": "Māwardī and al-Jubbāʾī offer this; Jubbāʾī says he could pray generally yet not know the particular food. Rāzī rejects this on prophetic certainty; al-Ālūsī finds his question awkward for the claim."}, {"id": "3:37/q34/p3", "position": "It was a sign anticipating Jesus' prophethood.", "reasons": "Al-Balkhī calls it a precursor; Māwardī relates it to the Messiah’s prophethood. Opponents say Jesus had not yet been born and the sign honors Mary."}, {"id": "3:37/q34/p4", "position": "No supernatural sign is required: ordinary believers could supply the food.", "reasons": "Al-Jubbāʾī suggests support for ascetics; Asad and Rashīd Riḍā question the evidence for miraculous legends. {"id": "3:37/q36", "question": "Who speaks the final statement about God's provision?", "turns_on": "Mary’s continued reply versus God’s own narration, with a joint-speech option.", "positions": [{"id": "3:37/q36/p1", "position": "Mary continues speaking.", "reasons": "Abū Ḥayyān, Ibn ʿĀshūr and al-Ālūsī prefer the apparent quotation; Ṭabrisī says it explains God’s free gift."}, {"id": "3:37/q36/p2", "position": "God begins a new statement to the Prophet or reader.", "reasons": "Ṭabarī says His stores cannot be depleted; Wāḥidī prefers a new sentence because the maxim is broader than the direct answer."}, {"id": "3:37/q36/p3", "position": "Zakariya and Mary speak it together.", "reasons": "Bayḍāwī offers a joint-speech alternative."}]}
{"id": "3:37/q37", "question": "What does 'without reckoning' mean?", "turns_on": "Immeasurable abundance, no earned entitlement or repayment, unexpected supply, or undiminished divine stores.", "positions": [{"id": "3:37/q37/p1", "position": "Abundant, unrestricted provision beyond enumeration.", "reasons": "Akhfash compares eating without a strict count; Zamakhsharī, Nasafī, Bayḍāwī, Biqāʿī and others describe limitless quantity."}, {"id": "3:37/q37/p2", "position": "A gracious gift without accounting for, entitlement from, or repayment for deeds.", "reasons": "Zamakhsharī and Nasafī contrast this with earned recompense; Qushayrī denies that worship causes provision or places an obligation on God."}, {"id": "3:37/q37/p3", "position": "God’s stores are not diminished and He needs no calculation or deliberation.", "reasons": "Ṭabarī says giving does not reduce divine dominion; Akhfash explains God's swift reckoning without thought; Study Quran adds that God answers to no one."}, {"id": "3:37/q37/p4", "position": "Provision arriving without a prior request or expected worldly cause.", "reasons": "Rāzī invokes 65:3; Bursevī includes unexpected sources."}]}
{"id": "3:37/q38", "question": "What legal or devotional lessons are drawn from Mary's care?", "turns_on": "", "positions": [{"id": "3:37/q38/p1", "position": "The guarantor assumes responsibility for another’s maintenance or debt.", "reasons": "Ṭabrisī explains the legal parties and debt; other sources cite the merit of caring for an orphan."}, {"id": "3:37/q38/p2", "position": "The maternal aunt has a mother-like claim in child custody.", "reasons": "Ibn Kathīr invokes the Prophet’s judgment concerning ʿImāra daughter of Ḥamza and her aunt."}]}
{"id": "3:37/q39", "question": "How does the passage link to neighboring verses and the sūra?", "turns_on": "", "positions": [{"id": "3:37/q39/p1", "position": "It fulfills Hanna’s prayer and anticipates Mary’s choosing and purity in 3:42.", "reasons": "Ibn ʿĀshūr notes the immediate reply; Ṭabāṭabāʾī links acceptance and growth to 3:42; Biqāʿī says the account clears confusion about Mary and Jesus."}, {"id": "3:37/q39/p2", "position": "The lot in 3:44 explains Zakariya’s custody, and his response leads into his prayer in 3:38.", "reasons": "Ṭabarī, Ibn ʿAṭiyya, Study Quran and others connect the scenes; Rāzī marks the turn from Hanna's account to Zakariya's."}, {"id": "3:37/q39/p3", "position": "Mary and Jesus are a sign for the worlds in 21:91, supporting the extraordinary-provision reading.", "reasons": "Zajjāj and Rāzī cite this verse; the latter argues an ordinary meal would not mark their sign."}]}
{"id": "3:37/q40", "question": "What parallel story is reported about Fatima's food?", "turns_on": "", "positions": [{"id": "3:37/q40/p1", "position": "Bread and meat multiplied for Fatima; she echoed Mary's answer when the Prophet asked its source.", "reasons": "Jābir’s versions differ in sequence and detail: a neighbor supplied food, a covered dish became full, the household ate, and the Prophet likened Fāṭima to Israel's foremost woman."}]}
{"id": "3:37/q41", "question": "What is the written and recited form of kullamā?", "turns_on": "", "positions": [{"id": "3:37/q41/p1", "position": "The codices normally write kullamā joined, including this verse.", "reasons": "Ibn al-Jazarī excepts the Ibrahim occurrence and notes disputed cases in other sūras; his general rule keeps joined words intact at a pause."}]}
{"id": "3:37/q42", "question": "Which vowel inclinations are transmitted near this verse?", "turns_on": "", "positions": [{"id": "3:37/q42/p1", "position": "The alif of ḥisāb permits imāla because of the preceding kasra.", "reasons": "Zajjāj and Naḥḥās report both full fatḥ and inclination."}, {"id": "3:37/q42/p2", "position": "Ibn Dhakwān inclines genitive miḥrāb, while accusative occurrences vary by route.", "reasons": "Ibn al-Jazarī distinguishes al-ʿImrān and Maryam genitives from disputed accusatives; Samīn notes local kasras."}]}

{"id": "3:44/q05", "question": "What does “We reveal it to you” mean, and what can waḥy denote?", "turns_on": "Whether the phrase is read as historical prophetic revelation or inward disclosure.", "positions": [{"id": "3:44/q05/p1", "position": "God communicates or sends this knowledge to Muhammad; waḥy broadly conveys meaning, often secretly, through revelation, inspiration, writing, gesture, speech, or a messenger.", "reasons": "Al-Ṭabarī glosses this instance ‘send down’ and catalogs bees (16:68), disciples (5:111), gesture (19:11), devilish suggestion (6:121), Gabriel's delivery (6:19), writing, and Kaʿb and Ruʾba's poetry. {"id": "3:44/q06", "question": "To what does the pronoun in “We reveal it” return?", "turns_on": "Whether the pronoun points to the demonstrative or to al-ghayb.", "positions": [{"id": "3:44/q06/p1", "position": "To “that,” the preceding account.", "reasons": "Al-Thaʿlabī, al-Jishumī, and al-Baghawī take the masculine pronoun from the demonstrative.
